für einen Zeitraum oder einen Menschen angeben, wie die/dessen Zeit genau verwendet werden soll; für einen Gegenstand festlegen, wie er verwendet/eingesetzt werden soll

examples.text: Jeder Tag des Urlaubs ist im Vorwege verplant.
Meine Sekretärin hat mich schon für die ganze nächste Woche verplant.
Nicht, dass du jetzt Eier isst, die sind alle schon zum Kuchenbacken für das Geburtstagsfest verplant.
„Weil wir oft schon vier Wochen im Voraus jedes Wochenende verplant haben, erst recht wenn Kinder da sind.“
„Aus Berliner Regierungskreisen verlautete jedoch am Freitag, zumindest der Bundesanteil an der Summe sei längst verplant oder werde zum Stopfen von Haushaltslöchern an anderer Stelle benötigt.“

glosses: beim Entwickeln eines Vorhabens (Plan) Fehler machen

examples.text: Da hast du dich wohl verplant, das passt ja gar nicht hier hinein!

glosses: The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or timeframe.

examples.text: limited budget
unlimited budget
tight budget
within the budget
over the budget

At the other extreme, with limitless budgets all they have to do is dream up amazing lighting rigs to be constructed and operated by the huge team of gaffers and sparks, with their generators, discharge lights, flags, gobos and brutes.
The latest Tory budget continued the trend begun in 2000 by making further small cuts in family income taxes.
The most common poly budget in use for games at the time of this writing is between 5,000 and 10,000 tris.

glosses: The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or timeframe.
A relatively small amount of available money.

examples.text: We're on a budget, so we can't afford to eat at that restaurant.

glosses: An itemized summary of intended expenditure; usually coupled with expected revenue.
A wallet, purse or bag.

examples.text: With that out of his bouget forth he drew / Great store of treasure, therewith him to tempt […]
The king holds up a hand to the lute player: ‘Thank you, leave us.’ The boy stuffs his music back into his budget and goes out backwards.

glosses: A compact collection of things.

examples.text: I set off, therefore, in high spirits, for I felt that I had done good work and was bringing back a fine budget of news for my companions.

glosses: A socket in which the end of a cavalry carbine rests.
Appropriate to a restricted budget.

examples.text: We flew on a budget airline.
A classic budget game, there isn't really anything outstanding about Rescue at all.

glosses: To construct or draw up a budget.

examples.text: Budgeting is even harder in times of recession

glosses: To provide funds, allow for in a budget.

examples.text: The PM’s pet projects are budgeted rather generously

glosses: To plan for the use of in a budget.

examples.text: The prestigious building project is budgeted in great detail, from warf facilities to the protocollary opening.

glosses: A drawing showing technical details of a building, machine, etc., with unwanted details omitted, and often using symbols rather than detailed drawing to represent doors, valves, etc.

examples.text: The plans for many important buildings were once publicly available.

glosses: A set of intended actions, usually mutually related, through which one expects to achieve a goal.

examples.text: He didn't really have a plan; he had a goal and a habit of control.
Life is what happens to you / While you're busy making other plans

glosses: A two-dimensional drawing of a building as seen from above with obscuring or irrelevant details such as roof removed, or of a floor of a building, revealing the internal layout; as distinct from the elevation.

examples.text: Seen in plan, the building had numerous passageways not apparent to visitors.

glosses: A method; a way of procedure; a custom.

examples.text: The simple plan, / That they should take who have the power, / And they should keep who can.

glosses: A subscription to a service.

examples.text: a phone plan
an Internet plan

glosses: To design (a building, machine, etc.).

examples.text: The architect planned the building for the client.

glosses: To create a plan for.

examples.text: They jointly planned the project in phases, with good detail for the first month.

glosses: To intend.

examples.text: He planned to go, but work intervened.
It has jailed environmental activists and is planning to limit the power of judicial oversight by handing a state-approved body a monopoly over bringing environmental lawsuits.

glosses: To make a plan.

examples.text: They planned for the worst, bringing lots of emergency supplies.

translations.source_sense_description: reflexiv: beim Entwickeln eines Vorhabens (Plan) Fehler machen
reflexiv: beim Entwickeln eines Vorhabens (Plan) Fehler machen

glosses: To calculate incorrectly.

examples.text: They miscalculated by assuming the dimensions were in imperial, not metric.

glosses: To make a gross error in judgment.

examples.text: Hitler and the Japanese generals miscalculated badly, 10 years ago, when they thought we would not be able to use our economic power effectively for the defeat of aggression. Let would-be aggressors make no such mistake today.

Obsessed only with cost, 'Sir Humphrey' saw that Transport for London 'got away' with ticket office closures on the Tube with only minor public pushback and miscalculated that it could do the same on the national network. This assumption backfired spectacularly.
